verdict_rationale.summary: V7 mechanism-level attack reveals that M3_REFINED's V6 'survival' (96.97% average) was based on the AVERAGE across 8 conditions, masking a 30% WORST-CASE reliability. Three independent failure modes were identified, each of which is a genuine engineering ceiling that cannot be resolved by parameter tuning or QC: (1) thermal activation window narrows with isolation degradation, (2) sensor electronics SPOF retains 8% invisible failures even with dual redundancy, (3) adhesion ceiling is biological (28% of patients exceed the snare's pull force capability). M3_REFINED as currently designed does NOT achieve buyer-grade reliability (≥95%) at worst case. The architecture must change to address these three failure modes. This is NOT a negative ceiling — the failure modes are potentially addressable by mechanism changes (electrothermal debonding, passive mechanical fallback, fever-aware activation). But V6's 'PROVISIONAL_SURVIVOR' verdict is DOWNGRADED to 'ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE_REQUIRED' — the current architecture cannot be declared a survivor.

v6_vs_v7_comparison.v7_verdict: ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE_REQUIRED — M3 fails ≥95% at worst case (30%)
v6_vs_v7_comparison.what_v6_missed: V6 reported the AVERAGE (96.97%) as the headline number. The worst case (30%) was buried in the details. V6 also assumed self-test detection was 60% (tested) but did not model the sensor electronics SPOF's impact on worst-case reliability. V7 shows that the 30% worst case is a REAL compound failure of three independent mechanisms, not a testing artifact.
v6_vs_v7_comparison.constitution_article_applied: Article XIX — 'Never optimize for the gate.' V6's 96.97% was obtained by averaging across conditions including easy ones (99% deployment). V7 attacks the worst case specifically.

failure_1_thermal_window.finding: At 6 months with isolation degradation (90%→50% efficiency), only Af=40°C SMA can reach activation temperature. Af=42°C and Af=43°C FAIL — the heater cannot overcome blood flow cooling + degraded isolation.
failure_1_thermal_window.implication: Af=40°C gives only 3°C margin above body temperature (37°C). Fever (38-39°C), exercise, or hot weather could trigger premature activation. The thermal window is too narrow for clinical safety.
failure_1_thermal_window.is_fixable: PARTIALLY — fever detection (don't activate if patient temperature >38°C) could mitigate, but adds complexity and a new failure mode (fever sensor failure).

failure_2_sensor_electronics_sPOF.finding: Dual-redundant sensors reduce invisible failures from 20% to 8% (common-mode: shared power, firmware, connector). 8% remains above the 5% threshold.
failure_2_sensor_electronics_sPOF.implication: 8% of SMA failures are invisible to the self-test. A clinician cannot know whether the self-test is working. This is unacceptable for a clinical device.
failure_2_sensor_electronics_sPOF.is_fixable: PARTIALLY — a passive mechanical fallback (no electronics, 88% reliability) could supplement. But passive alone is below 95%, and combined dual+passive still has ~5% residual (common-mode + passive failure).

failure_3_adhesion_ceiling.finding: The snare's maximum pull force (0.8N, limited by catheter tensile strength) is exceeded by 28% of patients' biological adhesion forces at 6 months. This is a DESIGN CEILING — adhesion is biological, not manufacturing.
failure_3_adhesion_ceiling.implication: 28% of patients CANNOT be retrieved with the current snare, regardless of QC. This is the dominant failure mode in the worst case (68/100 worst-case failures are 'adhesion_too_high').
failure_3_adhesion_ceiling.is_fixable: YES, by mechanism change — electrothermal debonding (heat to weaken tissue adhesion before pulling) could reduce adhesion below the snare's capability. But this is a DIFFERENT mechanism (M3 + debonding), not M3 alone.

T1_mechanism_robustness.result: Only Af=40°C works at 6mo (3°C margin above body temp). Af=42°C and 43°C FAIL.
T1_mechanism_robustness.verdict: FAIL — window is 3°C, not ≥8°C. Premature activation risk during fever/exercise.

T2_sensor_electronics_sPOF_resolution.result: Dual-redundant: 8% invisible (common-mode). Passive fallback: 88% alone, combined ~5% residual.
T2_sensor_electronics_sPOF_resolution.verdict: MARGINAL FAIL — 8% > 5% threshold even with dual redundancy. Passive fallback helps but doesn't fully resolve.

T3_manufacturing_variation_ceiling.result: Snare max = 0.8N. 72nd percentile adhesion = 0.8N. 28% of patients exceed snare capability.
T3_manufacturing_variation_ceiling.verdict: FAIL — design ceiling. 28% failure rate is biological, not fixable by QC.

T4_prior_art_novelty.target: §102 survives — no single reference teaches all limitations
T4_prior_art_novelty.result: Lens and Scopus searches returned 0 results for 'SMA CSF shunt retrieval' and 'nitinol thermal release implant'. The specific combination is not in the scholarly literature. V2 PatentBear audit (EP2043551B1, US11690741B2) found neighboring patents but none teaching electrothermal SMA phase-transition retrieval in CSF shunts.
T4_prior_art_novelty.verdict: PASS — §102 survives. The novelty distinction holds. But this is MOOT since the mechanism fails T1-T3.

T5_buyer_grade_reliability.result: Worst case = 30% (V6 confirmed). V7 shows this is a compound failure of three independent mechanisms.
T5_buyer_grade_reliability.verdict: FAIL — 30% << 95%. M3_REFINED does not achieve buyer-grade reliability at worst case.

what_would_overturn_this_verdict.if_electrothermal_debonding_is_added: If the mechanism is changed to include electrothermal debonding (heat to weaken adhesion before snare pull), the adhesion ceiling could be addressed. This is a V8 architecture change, not a V7 fix.
what_would_overturn_this_verdict.if_passive_mechanical_fallback_is_added: If a passive mechanical snare (no electronics) is added as a backup, the sensor SPOF could be mitigated. Combined dual-sensor + passive could achieve >95% if the passive is reliable enough.
what_would_overturn_this_verdict.if_fever_detection_is_added: If the system refuses to activate when patient temperature >38°C, the thermal window risk is mitigated. But this adds a new failure mode (fever sensor failure) and a new clinical constraint (can't retrieve during fever).

branch_disposition.change_reason: V7 mechanism attack reveals 3 independent failure modes that V6's 96.97% average masked. M3_REFINED as currently designed cannot achieve buyer-grade worst-case reliability.
branch_disposition.v8_authorized: CONDITIONAL — V8 may attempt to address the three failure modes through architecture changes (electrothermal debonding + passive fallback + fever detection). But V8 must NOT simply re-run V6 with adjusted parameters. The architecture must genuinely change.
branch_disposition.counts_toward_10_only_if: V8 architecture change achieves ≥95% worst-case reliability (not average) AND sensor SPOF is resolved to <5% invisible failures AND adhesion ceiling is addressed by debonding or equivalent.

constitution_compliance_check.article_VII_never_weaken_verifier: COMPLIED — did not lower the 95% threshold. Did not average away the worst case. Did not exclude difficult conditions.
constitution_compliance_check.article_XV_disclose_inconvenient_results: COMPLIED — the 30% worst case is surfaced as the primary finding, not buried.
constitution_compliance_check.article_XIX_never_optimize_for_gate: COMPLIED — V6's 96.97% was obtained by averaging. V7 attacks the worst case specifically. The 6-question test is answered below.

constitutional_test_6_questions.q1_what_was_previously_capable_of_killin: The 30% worst-case reliability was always visible in V6's data but was masked by the 96.97% average headline. The adhesion ceiling (28% failure), sensor SPOF (20% invisible), and thermal window narrowing were all present but not attacked at the mechanism level.
constitutional_test_6_questions.q2_what_changed: V7 attacked each failure mode at the mechanism level with first-principles physics. The 30% worst case is confirmed as a REAL compound failure, not a testing artifact.
constitutional_test_6_questions.q3_what_independent_evidence_shows_it_su: It did NOT survive. M3_REFINED fails at worst case. The verdict is ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE_REQUIRED, not SURVIVOR.
constitutional_test_6_questions.q4_what_is_still_capable_of_killing_it: If V8 adds electrothermal debonding, the adhesion ceiling may be resolved. If V8 adds passive fallback, the sensor SPOF may be mitigated. But both are architecture changes, not parameter adjustments.
constitutional_test_6_questions.q5_what_prevents_that_attack_now: The three failure modes are independent and compound. Fixing one (e.g., adhesion) does not fix the others (thermal, sensor). All three must be addressed simultaneously.
constitutional_test_6_questions.q6_did_the_fix_change_the_scientific_evi: V7 did not change the evidence — it ATTACKED the evidence. V6's 96.97% average was always misleading; V7 reveals the worst case that was always there. No parameters were tuned, no thresholds were lowered.

evidence_honesty_labels.thermal_model: FIRST_PRINCIPLES — body temperature (37°C), tissue damage threshold (45°C), ePTFE isolation degradation (90%→50% at 6mo) are published values. Blood flow cooling factor (30%) is an engineering estimate from venous sinus hemodynamics.
evidence_honesty_labels.sensor_redundancy_model: FIRST_PRINCIPLES — common-mode fraction (40%) is an engineering estimate based on shared power/firmware/connector analysis. Dual-redundant reduction (20%→8%) is derived from independent vs common-mode split.
evidence_honesty_labels.adhesion_model: PUBLISHED_LITERATURE — tissue adhesion force distribution (log-normal, mean 0.5N/cm², sigma 0.6) is from endovascular implant retrieval studies. Snare max pull force (0.8N) is from microcatheter tensile strength specifications.
evidence_honesty_labels.prior_art_search: API_VERIFIED — Lens (23,952 results for 'shape memory alloy', 0 for 'SMA CSF shunt retrieval') and Scopus (0 results for 'nitinol thermal retrieval implant') were queried with CEO-provided API keys. PatentBear has no public API (web scraping is documented substitute).

impact_on_portfolio.lesson: V6's 96.97% average masked a 30% worst case. ALWAYS report worst-case reliability for clinical devices. Averages are for engineering optimization; worst cases are for buyer-grade claims.
